title: Particle Wave Field
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a wave animation of 10,000 particles on a 100×100 grid.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Wave Mathematics]
(1) The particles are initially positioned in a regular 100×100 grid on the XZ plane (10000 points in total), with Y representing height.
(2) The height is the sum of three sine waves: h = A1*sin(f1*x + p1 + t*v) + A2*sin(f2*z + p2 + t*v) + A3*sin(f3*(x+z) + p3 + t*v) (the specific phases may be chosen freely, but the three terms must have independently adjustable frequencies/amplitudes).
(3) Particle colors are mapped according to height: low → blue, middle → white, high → red (gradients are allowed).

[Controls]
(4) Sliders id="wave1Amp", id="wave1Freq"; id="wave2Amp", id="wave2Freq"; id="wave3Amp", id="wave3Freq" (amplitude and frequency must use reasonable positive ranges, such as amp 0–2 and freq 0.1–3; the specific ranges must be labeled in the UI).
(5) The slider id="speed" controls time scaling or wave phase velocity.

[Mouse]
(6) When the mouse hovers/moves over the projection plane, it produces an additional local depression or bulge disturbance in nearby particles (with radial falloff).

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - particleCount: number (should be 10000)
  - wave1: { amp: number, freq: number }
  - wave2: { amp: number, freq: number }
  - wave3: { amp: number, freq: number }
  - speed: number
  - maxHeight: number (the maximum particle Y value or normalized height in the current frame)
  - minHeight: number (the minimum value in the current frame)

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
